entries.summary: The caller signs with its user seed.

account, user, ts and nonce in the signed input are the header values byte for byte, and subject is the header's sub.
The signed input hashes the raw payload, so an empty payload hashes to the SHA-256 of zero bytes.
The signature is ed25519 over the signed input, encoded base64url without padding, and the input itself is never sent.
The fixed first-line tag keeps a sender signature and an id_sig from being interchangeable.
By default the caller signs the very subject it publishes to.
When the caller's own account renamed an import, the caller signs the exporter's subject, not its local name.

No header, or an unknown v, makes the sender absent: the application sees absence, not an empty ID, and does no lookup.

The receiver also checks that sub is acceptable for the arrival subject.
The receiver also checks that ts lies within the replay window (default 30 seconds of skew).
The receiver also checks that the nonce has not been seen for this user within the window, keyed by user and nonce.

entries.summary: An implementing agent adds user_nkey, account and id_sig to the service metadata.
id_sig is an ed25519 signature by the user seed over the AGENT-ID-V1 input, base64url without padding.
The id_sig input uses the advertised prompt subject, not one derived from the instance name.
Identity metadata lacking a valid id_sig is only a claim.
A reverse lookup indexes records by account and user_nkey and keeps only instances whose id_sig verifies.
Implementations cache the reverse-lookup index briefly rather than enumerate per message.
An agent that holds its seed attaches Agent-Sender to every heartbeat.
entries.mutation: Publish an unsigned heartbeat on a host that holds a seed.

entries.summary: A signed heartbeat's sub is the heartbeat subject as published.
A signed heartbeat's ts is the heartbeat payload's own ts field.
A signed heartbeat's nonce is fresh for every heartbeat.
A signed heartbeat's sig covers the payload bytes as published, signed by the seed that signs id_sig.
Without a seed, the agent publishes heartbeats without the header, with the payload unchanged.
A subscriber discards a heartbeat that fails verification and never downgrades it to a claim.
The agent does not sign a reply, including a status reply.
entries.mutation: Sign a status reply.

entries.summary: A UI showing an identity also shows its trust class.
entries.not_applicable_reason: Informative display guidance in a security-considerations section.

entries.summary: An agent without identity support ignores an unknown Agent-Sender header and serves the request.
An agent with identity support serves a request without identity as an absent sender when the endpoint declares any.
An agent implements the extension if and only if its prompt metadata carries min_sender_trust.
The published known-answer sender signature vector reproduces byte for byte.
For session-aware harnesses each session is its own registration.
entries.not_applicable_reason: Informative appendix, explicitly non-normative.

entries.summary: A session-less harness may omit metadata.session or set it to default.
